title: Graceful Interruption Protocol and Cache‑First Eviction for SLO‑sensitive Continuous Batching
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Background: Continuous batching gives excellent throughput for steady request streams but makes preemption and KV cache management tricky because interrupting an in-flight slice can evict KV state and penalize downstream latency. Several prior tickets improved SLO accounting and soft-preemption heuristics, but we still see tenant unfairness and large latencies under mixed critical/noncritical workloads (see ENG-7421, ENG-21011 for context).

Goal: Implement an integrated "Graceful Interruption Protocol" (GIP) + Cache‑First Eviction policy that: (a) preserves tenant SLOs by bounding tail latency regressions during preemption, (b) reduces unnecessary KV cache churn (improving hit rates), and (c) enforces proportional fairness across tenants under GPU memory pressure. The feature should be rollout-safe (traffic experiments, canary) and observable via the Console dashboards.

Non‑Goals: Replacing global admission control; full rewrite of batching runtime; supporting every historical preemption variant in first iteration.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end 99th percentile latency increase <= 10% for P0 tenants under 60% GPU memory pressure compared to baseline in canary tests
KV cache global hit rate drop <= 5% during preemption storms versus baseline
Fairness metric (Jain's index across tenants' achieved throughput) improves by >= 8% under mixed workloads in synthetic 50-tenant test
Feature has a kill-switch: config flag to revert to previous preemption behavior and zero-downtime rollback plan
Telemetry emitted: preemptions_count, preemption_latency_impact_ms, kv_evictions_by_reason, gpu_mem_pressure_level, tenant_fairness_jain_index
design_notes:
High level components:
1) Preemption controller with Grace Window: when a slice is chosen to be preempted the controller issues a 'grace' signal (default 75ms) during which the runtime tries to finish critical KV flushes and write minimal continuation tokens instead of hard-cancel. Configurable per-priority band.

2) KV Residency Scorer: each KV shard maintains a lightweight score = alpha*access_freq + beta*recent_prefetch + gamma*tenant_priority_hint. When eviction is required, the scorer biases evictions toward cold keys and keys owned by low-priority tenants, but respects a small protected set for high-SLO tenants. Scores are decayed exponentially (tau=30s).

3) Cache‑First Evictor: instead of evicting tensors or compressing KV state first, the system attempts KV-only eviction pass. Only if KV eviction cannot free target bytes, we trigger tensor eviction/compaction and possible slice preemption. This preserves inference state locality and reduces rewarm cost.

4) Tenant Proportional Leak: To enforce fairness we maintain a soft token bucket per tenant representing accrued GPU allocation. When memory pressure spikes we proportionally throttle new batch admission using token balance. Tokens are replenished proportional to contracted capacity (Dedicated) or historical usage (hosted).

5) Safe Pause/Resume semantics: slices can be paused with a resumable checkpoint kept on fast host memory (pinned page cache) rather than fully evicted; resume paths attempt to rehydrate KV in-place if residency score allows.

6) Fallbacks and Rollout: automatic fallback to previous preemption mode when: >5x expected regression in 99p latency, or kv_hit_rate drops >10% for >2 minutes.

Implementation notes: controller is a new component in runtime/allocator; KV scorer lives in kv/cache_manager; eviction pipeline hooks added to mempressure path. We'll add unit tests for scorer and e2e bench harness in infra/perf.

decision_log: 2026-02-19: Chose grace-window=75ms default after microbench showing median continuation cost 40ms and max 120ms under 95th percentile. (design review)
2026-02-25: Adopted cache-first eviction vs tensor-first based on replayed preemption storms — KV rewarm cost was dominant in 60% of failures.
2026-03-03: Decided to use exponential decay tau=30s for KV score to capture working set shifts without oscillation.
2026-03-10: Opted for proportional token replenishment by contracted capacity (Dedicated) and 95th-percentile recent usage for hosted. This simplifies fairness during bursty tenants.
test_plan:
Unit tests: KV scorer correctness, eviction ordering deterministic under seeded RNG.
Integration tests: synthetic mixed-priority workload produces expected eviction targets and no regressions vs base preemption.
Perf canary: deploy to one dedicated pool (~8 GPUs) with 50 synthetic tenants (mix of P0/P2) for 24 hours. Measure 50/90/95/99 latencies and kv hit rates.
Observability: Dashboard panels for preemptions_count, preemption_latency_impact_ms, kv_evictions_by_reason. Automated alert if 99p latency > baseline*1.1 for >5m.
Rollback plan: gate feature behind runtime flag and k8s rollout, allow immediate toggle and scale down to 0 variants on failure.
